questions.question: A certain amount of money at compound interest grows to ₹66,550 in 3 years and ₹73,205 in 4 years. The rate percent per annum is:
questions.solution:
Step 1   Take the difference. 
73,205 − 66,550 = ₹6,655 
 Step 2   Measure it on the 3-year amount. 
6,655 / 66,550 × 100 = 10%

questions.question: The difference between the compound interest on a sum of ₹8,000 for 1 year at the rate of 10% per annum, interest compounded yearly and half yearly is: ₹8,000
questions.solution:
Step 1   Layers. 
5% of 8,000 = 400      5% of 400 = 20 
 Step 2   The difference is the last layer. 
(800 + 20) − 800 = ₹20

questions.question: The simple interest on a sum at 3% per annum in 3 years is ₹315. What will be the compound interest on this amount compounded annually at the rate of 4% per annum for 2 years?
questions.solution:
Step 1   One year of simple interest. 
315 / 3 = ₹105 a year, which is 3% of P   ∴  P = 
₹3,500 
 Step 2   Now 2 years at 4%, row 2 : 1. 
4% of 3,500 = 140      4% of 140 = 5.6 
 Step 3   Add the layers. 
2(140) + 5.6 = ₹285.60

questions.question: The difference in compound interest on a certain sum at 10% p.a. for one year, when the interest is compounded half yearly and yearly, is ₹88.80. What is the simple interest on the same sum for 1⅔years at the same rate?
questions.solution:
Step 1   Yearly against half-yearly, one year. 
yearly = 10x        half-yearly (5% twice) = 10x + 
0.25x = 10.25x 
 Step 2   The gap is the extra quarter-unit. 
0.25x = 88.80   ⇒  x = 355.2   ∴  P = ₹35,520 
 Step 3   Simple interest for 1⅓ years at 10%. 
35,520 × 10 × (4/3) / 100 = ₹4,736

questions.question: When interest is compounded annually, the amount of money in a bank account doubles in 7 years. How many years will it take to multiply this amount in the bank 8 times?
questions.solution:
Step 1   Express 8 times as doublings. 
8 = 2³  ⇒  three doubling periods 
 Step 2   Each doubling takes 7 years. 
3 × 7 = 21 years

questions.question: Divide ₹66300 between A and B such that the amount received by A after 8 years is equal to the amount received by B after 10 years. Whereas the rate of interest is 10% per annum compounded annually. ₹66300
questions.solution:

A(1.1)⁸ = B(1.1)¹⁰   ⇒  A / B = (1.1)² = 121 / 100

221 parts = 66,300 ⇒ 1 part = 300   ∴  A =

questions.question: A person borrowed a sum of ₹30,800 at 10% per annum for 3 years. Interest compounded annually. At the end of the second year, he paid a sum of ₹13268. At the end of IIIrd year he paid Rs. x to clear of the debt. Find the value of x.
questions.solution:
Step 1   Two years of growth, row 2 : 1. 
10% of 30,800 = 3,080,  of 3,080 = 308   ⇒  
interest = ₹6,468,  amount = ₹37,268 
 Step 2   He pays ₹13,268 at that point. 
37,268 − 13,268 = ₹24,000 still owed 
 Step 3   One more year on the balance. 
x = 24,000 × 1.1 = ₹26,400

questions.question: For a fixed period an amount of Rs. 60,000 invested at a fixed rate. The amount, whose interest is compounded annually, has increased to Rs. 63,654. If at the same rate, the amount would have been invested for half of the duration, how much would it have increased? ₹60,000
questions.solution:
Step 1   Divide. 
63,654 / 60,000 = 1.0609 = (1.03)²   ⇒  3% a 
period over 2 periods 
 Step 2   Half the duration is one period. 
60,000 × 1.03 = ₹61,800   ⇒  increase = ₹1,800
